principle_violations.reason: The Order class is not only managing the order data (items, quantities, prices) but is also responsible for modifying the order status. Similarly, the PaymentProcessor class should only focus on processing payments and not modify the order's state directly.
principle_violations.suggestion: Extract the status management from the Order class, and create a separate class to manage the Order state transitions. The PaymentProcessor can utilize this to change the status instead of doing it directly.

principle_violations.reason: The Pay method in the PaymentProcessor class has a direct dependency on the Order class. This ties the PaymentProcessor to a specific implementation of order management.
principle_violations.suggestion: Create an interface or abstract class for order management, which can be implemented by different types of order classes. This way, PaymentProcessor would depend on the abstraction rather than a concrete implementation.

overall_feedback: 2 principle violations found. Please see the details below.
